claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is single-phase BCC.
The initial alloy has dendritic/interdendritic micro-segregation that produces asymmetric XRD peaks.
The initial alloy exhibits low room-temperature fracture strain.
Approximately 4 at.% Cr is added to the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
Homogenization at approximately 1200°C for 24 hours permits phase separation while retaining an interdendritic network.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces a complex C14 or C15 Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase is enriched in Hf and Cr.
The Laves phase forms a reticulated, interconnected morphology preferentially at interdendritic boundaries.
The Cr-induced Laves phase occupies between 3% and 5% of the alloy volume.
The interconnected Laves phase is brittle and acts as a crack-initiation site.
The interconnected Laves phase provides a continuous crack-propagation path that bypasses crack bridging or deflection.
Cr dissolved in the BCC matrix causes lattice distortion.
Cr dissolved in the BCC matrix causes net lattice-parameter contraction because Cr has a smaller atomic radius than Hf, Zr, and Ti.
Cr-induced lattice distortion produces solid-solution hardening and increases yield strength.
Cr-induced hardening reduces strain-hardening capacity and promotes early fracture.
The Cr-containing alloy will have fracture strain that remains low or decreases relative to the Cr-free baseline.
The BCC (110) XRD peak will shift to higher 2θ because of lattice contraction.
Weak Laves-phase peaks will appear in the XRD pattern.
Fracture will proceed intergranularly along the interdendritic Laves network.
The mechanism requires Cr to exceed its BCC-matrix solubility limit and fails if Cr remains fully dissolved or forms a different phase such as sigma.

contradictions.description: The query requires the reticulated secondary phase to impede crack extension, whereas the proposed mechanism says that the interconnected brittle phase supplies a continuous path that facilitates crack propagation and bypasses crack-deflection or crack-bridging mechanisms.
